title: Model resolution contract: tag/semver/commit semantics in SDK
creator: Asha Menon
description: We need a clear, predictable model resolution contract for SDK/API clients that supports: tag-based pins (eg 'stable', 'gpu-quant'), semver ranges (eg '^1.4.0' / '>=1.2 <2.0'), and absolute references (commit hashes or immutable build ids). Right now clients use ad-hoc strings and the platform resolves inconsistently across hosted/dedicated/private deployments. This causes rollout surprises, flaky benchmarks, and user confusion when performance profiles change between minor releases. Goal: define resolution semantics, precedence rules, and SDK helper APIs so customers can pin models deterministically and we can publish performance profiles that unambiguously map to the serving artifact used at inference time.
proposal: Introduce a model selector grammar and deterministic resolution order. Selector forms: 1) name:tag (e.g., 'redwood/guanaco:stable') resolves to the latest model build annotated with tag 'stable' at the time of resolution. 2) name@semver (e.g., 'redwood/guanaco@^1.2.0') supports npm-style semver operators: ^, ~, >=, <=, exact. 3) name#commit (e.g., 'redwood/guanaco#f3a1b2c') resolves to the immutable build with that commit id or build id. Precedence when multiple selectors could match: when a client passes an exact commit (#) it wins. When passing a tag and semver simultaneously via newer selector syntax (see API examples), explicit commit overrides both. Default unspecified form: legacy shorthand (just 'redwood/guanaco') resolves to 'name:latest' where 'latest' is an implicit tag that tracks the most recent GA build and should be used sparingly for production workloads. SDK helpers: Model.resolve(selector) returns a resolution object with resolved_model_id, resolved_tag(s), resolved_semver, and performance_profile_id. The server will return a stable mapping at resolution time and include an 'etag' and 'resolved_at' timestamp in the response so clients can log exact provenance for each inference request. Backwards compatibility: old callers that pass plain strings behave as before but we will start returning the resolution metadata to encourage migration. We will not change default semantics without a major announcement and a migration window.
api_examples: HTTP: POST /v1/infer with body {"model": "redwood/guanaco@^1.4.0", "inputs": [...]} => server resolves the highest matching semver tag that is compatible and returns 'x-model-resolved: redwood/guanaco@1.4.3 (build b123, profile p-98)' header.

HTTP: POST /v1/infer with body {"model": "redwood/guanaco:staging", "inputs": [...]} => resolves to the most recent build annotated 'staging'; response includes 'x-resolved-commit' and performance_profile id.

New selector form: 'name|tag@semver' allows expressing priorities when needed: e.g., 'redwood/guanaco|stable@^1.4.0' will prefer tag 'stable' but only if it satisfies semver '^1.4.0', otherwise fallback rules apply. This is optional and primarily for advanced rollout control.
acceptance_criteria: SDK exposes a stable Model.resolve(selector) that returns resolved_model_id, resolved_commit, resolved_semver, resolved_tags, performance_profile_id, etag, and resolved_at (all strings).
API inference responses include headers: x-resolved-model, x-resolved-commit, x-performance-profile, x-resolved-at for any request that includes a model selector.
Server-side resolution implements semver operators ^, ~, >=, <= and exact equality; resolves deterministically (documented algorithm).
Compatibility: existing plain-model-name requests continue to work and now receive resolution metadata in responses (no behavioral change).
Docs and SDK changelog updated with migration guidance and examples.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (SDK alpha): add Model.resolve and response headers; opt-in flag --sdk-experimental-model-resolution in SDK; run internal smoke tests. (2 weeks)
Phase 2 (Server): enable resolution for hosted and dedicated with feature flag 'model_resolution_v2'. Private deploy customers can opt-in. (2 weeks)
Phase 3 (Migration): enable metadata headers by default, monitor for customers relying on previous implicit behavior; announce GA and recommend using semver or commit pins for production. (1 week)
Phase 4 (Docs/Training): update quickstarts, release notes, and run office hours with top customers. (ongoing)
migration_notes: Recommend customers pin critical routes to commit (#) or exact semver (e.g., @1.4.3) before changing default behavior in any environment.
Provide a small CLI tool to map existing tag names to current commit ids and performance profiles to ease migration for Dedicated/Private customers.
Mark 'latest' as unstable in docs and show warnings in Console for routes using unqualified model names.
testing_plan: Unit tests: semver parser, selector grammar, resolution precedence matrix with corner cases.
Integration tests: simulate hosted + dedicated registries with overlapping tags and semver ranges; assert deterministic picks.
E2E: run performance profile publishing flow and verify inference responses include matching performance_profile_id and token latency bounds.
Chaos: during canary rollout, inject a competing publish to the same tag and assert resolution uses timestamp-based tie-breaker documented in algorithm.
risks_mitigation: Risk: customers rely on implicit rolling behavior for 'stable' tag. Mitigation: emit deprecation warning in Console and SDK when using implicit tags; provide migration window and automation to pin to commit.
Risk: semver parsing differences across languages. Mitigation: re-use existing canonical semver library in server and SDKs; add cross-language golden test vectors.

Risk: performance profile mismatch if model binary rotated after resolution. Mitigation: resolution response includes performance_profile_id; runtime will refuse to serve incompatible binary that lacks published profile snapshot.
references: Related Linear: ENG-7351 (pin-policy SDK API versioning)
